# SpectraSort

> SpectraSort is an iOS photo finder. Six one-tap tools surface the photos you actually want — your best shots, a favorite subject, the ones only you would pick — and it learns your eye as it goes. Everything runs on your iPhone; photos never leave it.

SpectraSort solves the finding problem: you have thousands of photos but no easy way to surface the ones worth keeping, sharing, or looking at again. One fast on-device engine, three ways in — one-tap tools, a browsable library, a studio of controls.

## Toolbox — six one-tap tools

Each tool is pointed at a different photo you're looking for:

- **Your Taste** — a profile built from the photos you keep and the ones you let go. Run it and the top of the pile starts looking like the photos you'd have picked yourself. Learning can be paused or reset at any time; the profile never leaves the device.
- **Best Shots** — your sharpest, best-exposed, best-composed photos first, with a slider to lean the ranking technical or artistic.
- **Find a Subject** — free-text photo search. Concrete ("roses"), compound ("dogs at the beach"), or abstract ("cozy", "golden hour") — the phrase is matched against your photos on the phone.
- **Like This Photo** — point at one photo, get everything like it. On-device similar-photo search.
- **Photos of a location** — pin a place on a map, see everything shot there.
- **Dedupe** — exact duplicates, shots in a series, and near-identical look-alikes gathered into stacks to clear. Grouping is controlled per type (Duplicates, Sequence, Similar) or turned off.

## Discover

Face a big library one piece at a time. Scenes gather trips, themes, and series automatically; a Timeline browses year to month to day. Any slice can be sorted with a tap.

## Review

After a sort, the best photos rise to the top — "best" meaning whatever the tool was asked for — with look-alikes stacked. Swipe right to Pick, down to Keep, left to Discard; or let Autopick sort them. Nothing is applied until an action is tapped. Batch Process finishes the job: picks to an album or the share sheet, the rest deleted only on explicit confirmation through the system Photos dialog.

## Studio (Premium)

Full manual control: seven quality sliders (sharpness, exposure, contrast, noise, composition, color harmony, visual balance), a weight wheel that splits subject relevance against raw quality, and up to three subjects at once — even a photo as a subject. Settings save as profiles; profiles can be bookmarked for quick switching.

Profile types: **Taste** (auto-built from your picks), **Custom** (dialed in by hand in Studio), **Bookmarked** (starred for quick access).

## Speed

The first sort indexes the library on Apple's Neural Engine — up to 100 photos per second — one time. Every sort after runs on that index and lands nearly instantly.

## How it compares

| Feature                       | SpectraSort | Apple Photos | Google Photos |
|-------------------------------|-------------|--------------|---------------|
| AI quality scoring            | Yes         | No           | Limited       |
| Learns personal taste         | Yes (on-device) | No       | Partial (cloud) |
| Free-text photo search        | Yes (on-device) | Limited  | Yes (cloud)   |
| Similar-photo search          | Yes (on-device) | No       | No            |
| On-device processing          | Yes         | Yes          | No (cloud)    |
| No account required           | Yes         | Yes          | No            |
| Swipe interface for picking   | Yes         | No           | No            |
| Bulk actions after review     | Yes         | Manual       | Manual        |

SpectraSort is the only iOS photo app that combines free-text search, similar-photo search, quality scoring, and personalized taste learning entirely on-device.

## Pricing

Five free sorts a week, for everyone — not a trial. Saving, sharing, and deleting results is always free.

- **Premium** — $19.99, one-time purchase. Removes the weekly sort limit and unlocks Studio. No subscription, no renewals.

Premium can be restored on any device signed in with the same Apple ID. Purchases from SpectraSort 2.x carry over automatically.

## Privacy

Everything happens on the device using Apple's Neural Engine and Core ML. There are no photo uploads, no cloud processing, no account, and no analytics on photo content.

The only data collected is anonymous app-usage analytics (Firebase Analytics + Crashlytics) and only when the user opts in. The toggle defaults to off in the EU, UK, and EEA; it defaults to on elsewhere but can be turned off at any time in Settings → Privacy. The analytics never include photo data, locations, or anything that could identify the user — only event names like "sort started" and crash diagnostics.
